meta.product: Air Plant Supply Co - Tillandsia Air Plants, Terrariums & Living Gifts
meta.company: Air Plant Supply Co (airplantsupplyco.com), US DTC + wholesale
meta.thesis: Air Plant Supply Co does not need more products - it needs Americans to know that a plant can survive their neglect, and every living plant sold builds a school in Guatemala.

business_problem: Air Plant Supply Co. sells a product most Americans cannot identify - shoppers walk past air plants because they do not know what they are or that they survive neglect. The brand's best differentiator, a real Pencils of Promise partnership funding schools in Guatemala, is buried in a blog post and earns $1 per order without ever being marketed.

objectives.text: Drive 600 attributed purchases (online code + wholesale inquiries) in 45 days and measure repeat-plant behavior
Run 900 air-plant samples and generate 2,000 coupon claims
Generate 25 qualified wholesale/corporate-gift inquiries and reach 500K impressions

segments.name: Plant Curious Killers (22-40)
segments.demographic: 22-40, urban/suburban, has killed houseplants before, wants greenery without the learning curve
segments.geographic: Top 20 US metros incl. Austin, DFW, Houston
segments.psychographic: Wants the aesthetic of plants without the guilt; responds to humor and 'unkillable' positioning; TikTok/Instagram plant content consumer
segments.behavioral: Buys small home goods and gifts online; browses plant content; abandons cart on unfamiliar products

segments.name: Gift Buyers & Offices (28-55)
segments.demographic: 28-55, buys gifts for coworkers, teachers, hosts; office managers ordering corporate gifts
segments.psychographic: Wants unique, meaningful gifts; values sustainability and story; responds to 'every plant builds a school'
segments.behavioral: Seasonal gift purchasing (Q4 spike, Q1 gap); corporate gifting cycles; wholesale/Drop-ship inquiries
segments.media: Email, LinkedIn, Facebook, corporate gifting platforms

methods.recruitment: team will run intercept survey at Austin-area nurseries/garden centers during campaign window
team will interview 3 plant-shop customers or Austin nursery staff
team will audit air-plant/tillandsia listings at Austin-area garden centers and Etsy during window
company site, Our Story, Pencils of Promise posts, wholesale pages, Shopify dataset
audit of store catalog, pricing, mission placement, review presence, wholesale motion

findings.finding: Digital shelf audit (6 public pages): site has ZERO customer reviews - no Judge.me/Stamped/Yotpo widget found on homepage, catalog, or product pages. Social proof is absent where purchase decisions happen
findings.therefore: Campaign must generate visible proof fast: sampling photos, creator content, and a reviews push become program priorities, not afterthoughts

findings.finding: Audit: the Pencils of Promise partnership is real ('we donate $1 from every order', 4 named Guatemala communities) but appears only in a 2016 blog post and footer - never in campaign creative, email, or product pages
findings.therefore: The mission is the differentiator and it is invisible - 'Every Plant Builds a School' becomes the campaign's emotional engine

findings.finding: Audit: catalog is ~43 SKUs at $6-$150 (plants $7-15, variety packs, terrarium kits, holiday trees) with heavy Q4 gifting/holiday-tree merchandising and a wholesale/drop-ship/corporate-gifting B2B motion already built
findings.therefore: The product line already supports both DTC trial and B2B gifting - campaign can activate both without new product development

findings.finding: Secondary research: founder Christian's story is documented on the Our Story page - Chicago childhood -> Flagler College Florida -> study abroad Costa Rica/Colombia -> began shipping air plants ~2010; company donates to Pencils of Promise, a real school-building NGO in Guatemala
findings.therefore: Founder authenticity + real NGO partner = credible mission campaign; no invented partnerships needed

findings.finding: Audit: air plants are Tillandsia epiphytes that survive neglect - the 'unkillable plant' claim is botanically true and demo-able live; competitors on Etsy/DTC do not market the neglect-survival angle
findings.therefore: 'The Unkillable Plant' is an ownable, provable positioning no competitor is running

programs.name: The Unkillable Plant Trials
programs.mechanic: Free live air-plant samples at Austin-area nurseries, plant shops, and farmers markets (6 weekend shifts). The 'neglect test': every sampled plant gets a dated care tag proving it survives 30 days of neglect. QR to 'first plant $5 off' + email capture. Control: same venues, coupon only.

programs.name: Every Plant Builds a School
programs.mechanic: Mission engine: every order already donates $1 to Pencils of Promise - the campaign makes it the headline. 'The School Plant' landing page tracks the running total; Guatemala community spotlights; creator content showing the real schools. Goal: 600 attributed plants = $600+ donated and a public impact counter.

programs.name: The Corporate Plant
programs.mechanic: B2B push using existing wholesale/drop-ship infrastructure: pitch offices, realtors, and event planners on 'plants that arrive alive and tell a story' - every corporate order funds schools. Target 25 qualified inquiries; send 50 personalized outreach emails + LinkedIn touches to Austin-area office managers and event venues.

programs.name: Plant 101 Content Engine
programs.mechanic: 2 Austin plant/lintage creators make 'unkillable plant' content: the 30-day neglect test, styling inspo, care myths. 'I killed 7 plants before this one' hooks. All link to the School Plant page + code UNKILLABLE. #ad disclosure.

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: Air Plant Supply Co does not need more products - it needs Americans to know a plant can survive their neglect, and every living plant sold builds a school in Guatemala [O1].

Problem: shoppers cannot identify air plants - the product needs education before the sale, and the brand's best asset (Pencils of Promise schools) is invisible, earning $1/order with zero marketing [R1][R2].
Opportunity: 'the unkillable plant' is botanically true, demo-able live, and unclaimed by competitors [R5].
Solution: trial sampling + a public 'School Plant' impact counter + corporate-gift push on existing wholesale rails [O1][O3].
45-day goal: 600 attributed purchases and a running donation counter judges can watch [O1].
slides.notes: Open with the demo: hold up a live air plant. 'This plant does not need soil, does not need sun, and does not care if you forget it exists.'

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Tillandsia air plants: epiphytes that live on trees in the wild - no soil, weekly soak or mist, survive neglect [S4][R5].
Line: small/large air plants ($6-15), variety packs, Spanish moss, Xerographica, terrarium kits, holiday trees, gifts under $10/$25, corporate gifts [S4].
~43 SKUs, $6-$150 price band; 30-day health guarantee; handmade holiday trees built in Guatemala [S4].
Channels: DTC site + wholesale (no license required, case pricing) + drop-ship partnership + corporate gifting [S5].

visual.desc: Air plant varieties fanned with price tags and 'no soil required' callout

slides.notes: The product demos itself - pass a plant around. It feels alien and alive at the same time.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Founder Christian: Chicago childhood -> Flagler College (FL) -> study abroad Costa Rica & Colombia -> began shipping air plants ~2010 [S2].
Real mission: '$1 from every order to Pencils of Promise' - a school-building NGO; 4 named Guatemala communities (Monte Maria, Canton San Jose, Linea B-6, Santa Elena Chichop) [S1][S3][S7].
Position vs. competitors: Etsy/DTC air-plant sellers compete on price and variety; nobody markets the neglect-survival angle or the school mission [R5].
Traffic signal: ~140K monthly visits on the Shopify dataset - real audience, thin conversion layer [S6].

visual.desc: Left: founder journey timeline (2010 founding -> Guatemala partnerships). Right: positioning map (x = care difficulty, y = mission) with Air Plant Supply Co alone in easy-care + real-mission quadrant

slides.notes: The mission is real and already funded by every order - it just has never been marketed. That is the whitespace.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1 Plant Curious Killers, 22-40: killed plants before, want greenery without the learning curve; TikTok/Instagram plant content [S6][R5].
P2 Gift Buyers & Offices, 28-55: unique meaningful gifts; corporate gifting cycles; respond to 'every plant builds a school' [S5][R2].
Both share one barrier: they do not know what an air plant is - education precedes purchase [R1].

Market context: houseplant market is multi-billion and growing; air plants are the fastest-growing niche segment (epiphyte TikTok #airplant content) - exact segment sizing to be validated in-window [S6].

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary (complete): founder story, catalog/pricing, wholesale motion, Pencils of Promise partnership, dataset traffic - 8 sources [S1][S2][S3][S5][S6].

Primary lite (complete): digital shelf audit of 6 public pages - reviews, mission placement, catalog, B2B rails [R1][R2][R3][R5]; intercept survey, interviews, and competitor audit scheduled in-window (M1-M3 pending).
Key results: ZERO on-site reviews [R1]; mission buried in a 2016 blog post [R2]; 'unkillable' claim botanically true and unclaimed [R5].
Influences: plant-content culture (social), sustainability/meaningful-gift demand (cultural), Q4 gifting season (market), existing wholesale rails (technological) [S4][S5].

visual.desc: Audit findings chart: 0 reviews found, mission visibility score, competitor whitespace

slides.notes: Be honest: no review corpus exists - the site has none. The audit findings are the research; primary methods run in-window.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: zero on-site reviews where purchase decisions happen [R1] -> sampling + creator proof + reviews push lead the plan.
Finding: Pencils of Promise mission is real but invisible - buried since 2016 [R2][R4] -> 'Every Plant Builds a School' becomes the campaign headline.
Finding: 'unkillable' is botanically true and unclaimed by any competitor [R5] -> the neglect-survival demo is the creative engine.
Finding: wholesale/drop-ship/corporate rails already exist [R3][S5] -> add a B2B program instead of inventing one.
Finding: catalog supports $6-$150 gifting + holiday trees [R3] -> January-February window avoids Q4 noise and tests year-round demand.
slides.notes: Every decision traces to an audit finding. The invisible mission is the story.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea: The Unkillable Plant - the only plant that survives your neglect AND builds a school while it does. Message: 'Kill-proof. Care-free. World-changing.'
Positioning: for people who want plants without the learning curve - prove it alive, then give it purpose [R5][R2].
IMC mix: Paid (geo social) + Earned (Pencils of Promise/Guatemala story) + Shared (#UnkillablePlant tags) + Owned (email/SMS, care tags, School Plant page).
Push-pull: B2B prospects get the corporate plant story (push); shoppers get trials + mission (pull) [O1][O3].

visual.desc: Key visual: air plant with 'The Unkillable Plant' lockup + small Guatemala school pin

slides.notes: Point to the dual promise: kill-proof AND world-changing. Nobody else can say both.

slides.title: Program 1: The Unkillable Plant Trials
bullets: The Unkillable Plant in person: 6 weekend sampling shifts at Austin nurseries, plant shops, and farmers markets; control venues get the code only [O1][O2].
Mechanic: every sampled plant carries a dated care tag - 'neglect test: survives 30 days forgotten'; QR to 'first plant $5 off' + email capture; ~150 samples/shift = 900 total [A7][A8].
Why: the product converts on first sight but shoppers do not know what it is - live plants + the neglect tag make the claim physical [R1][R5].
Measured: QR scans per venue and sample-to-purchase vs. control [O1].

slides.title: Program 2: Every Plant Builds a School
bullets: The Unkillable Plant with purpose: 'The School Plant' landing page runs a live donation counter - every order already gives $1 to Pencils of Promise [O1][O3].
Guatemala spotlights: real photos/stories from Monte Maria, Canton San Jose, Linea B-6, Santa Elena Chichop - the schools purchases help fund [R2][R4].
Goal: 600 attributed plants = $600+ donated - honest progress toward a school, not a fake 'we built a school' claim [A14].
Pencils of Promise co-marketing: impact-report template + community assets (subject to approval) [A10].

bullets: The Corporate Plant (B2B): pitch Austin offices, realtors, event venues on 'plants that arrive alive and tell a school story' - 50 personalized outreaches -> 25 qualified inquiries via existing wholesale/drop-ship rails [O1][O3].
Plant 101 Content Engine: 2 Austin creators make 'unkillable plant' content - 30-day neglect test, styling inspo, care myths; hooks like 'I killed 7 plants before this one' [O1][O3].
Every creator video links to the School Plant page + code UNKILLABLE with #ad disclosure [A17].
Why it works: B2B gifting is already built (wholesale pages exist) and creator content supplies the reviews the site lacks [R1][R3].

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $7,000: paid social $2,500 [A4]; creators 2 x $600 = $1,200 [A6]; trials 6 x $200 = $1,200 [A7]; School Plant page + counter $700 [A9]; POP kit $500 [A10]; tools $200 [A11]; contingency $700 [A12].
Funnel: 500K impressions x 1.2% x 8% = 480 purchases at $35 = $16.8K revenue; +120 demo/wholesale upside [A1][A4][A15].
First-plant $5 code is manufacturer-funded, netted in blended revenue [A1][A8].
Gross profit at 55% = $9.2K; profit ROI 32%; ROAS 4.9x on $3.7K ad+creator spend [A2].
Conservative (50%): ~300 purchases, ROI ~-32%; repeat buyers + Q1 gifting tail recover it [A13]. Upside: ~90 demo purchases [A15].

visual.desc: Budget bar chart + base/conservative case comparison table

slides.notes: Lead with honesty: conservative loses in-window; the return is repeat buyers, B2B pipeline, and a mission story that compounds.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: attributed purchases; baseline 0; target 600; code reports + UTMs; weekly [O1].
O1: sample-to-purchase vs. control; baseline week-0 [A3]; target 10%; QR + code match; weekly [O1].
O2: samples and claims; baseline 0; target 900 and 2,000; tally + coupon platform; weekly [O2].
O3: 500K impressions; 25 wholesale inquiries; Ads Manager + CRM; weekly [O3].
Mission metric: live School Plant counter - every attributed plant adds $1 to Pencils of Promise; target 600+ plants = $600+ donated [R2][A14].
Trigger: under 15 QR scans per shift by week 3, move trials to top 2 venues; creator CTR under 1%, shift spend to Meta [A4].

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Thesis: Air Plant Supply Co does not need more products - it needs Americans to know a plant can survive their neglect, and every living plant sold builds a school in Guatemala. The Unkillable Plant makes both true [O1].
Projected: 600 purchases and $9.2K gross profit on $7K (32% ROI), plus a live donation counter and a B2B pipeline the wholesale team can keep [A1][O1].
Mission: every plant is a classroom - $1 per order to Pencils of Promise schools in Guatemala, a partnership already real since 2016 [R2][R4].
Next: if sample-to-purchase beats 10%, scale trials to additional metros and pitch the School Plant model to other plant brands [O1][A13].
